title: Orchestration rulebook for fractional model intake
creator: Ava Chen
description: Implement a config-driven policy engine and orchestration 'rulebook' to support fractional (percent-based) model intake: traffic splits, multi-step schedules, shadow probes, canary guardrails, and automatic rollback triggers. This ticket focuses on the configuration schema, runtime validation, and a minimal implementation path to enable product teams to define safe fractional rollouts without engineering intervention for each release.
context: Customers require predictable model switches: staged percentages, automatic regressions, and the ability to shadow a new model at 100% without impacting production. Current rollout primitives are ad-hoc scripts and per-service code. We need a centralized engine that evaluates policies and drives traffic routers, with strong observability and easy authoring in the Console.
proposed_solution: 1) Define a compact YAML/JSON config schema for 'rulesets' capturing steps, durations, stop-conditions, and guardrails (latency, error rate, quality regressions). 2) Implement a stateless validator in API layer and a controller that emits desired traffic split adjustments to the router. 3) Add a 'shadow mode' toggle that mirrors sampled traffic to the candidate model. 4) Wire up telemetry: per-step metrics and a canary health score computed from existing traces and eval prompts. 5) Support auto-rollback: policy DSL can specify thresholds and cooldowns. 6) Expose the rulebook editor in Console as a controlled feature flag.
decisions: Use percentage-based fractional steps with optional fixed-duration or metric-gated advancement
Keep policy evaluation in the control plane; router receives only signed 'desired split' deltas
Shadow traffic will be strictly sample-based with explicit customer opt-in
Auto-rollback triggers will be multi-metric: p95 latency, 5xx rate, and quality eval delta
tradeoffs: Centralized engine increases blast radius if misconfigured -> mitigate with signed manifests and enforced dry-run for first deployment
Keeping evaluation in control plane simplifies rollout but adds control-plane load; we'll limit policy evaluation frequency and cache results
Full A/B analysis (stat significance) is out of scope for first iteration; we'll rely on threshold-based gating
tasks: Design rulebook schema and examples (this ticket)
Implement schema validator and parser in api/runtime (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1182)
Controller to compute and emit split deltas to router (ENG-47322 will own router integration)
Shadow sampling implementation and opt-in plumbing in API (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/api/pull/460)
Telemetry: add canary health score aggregator and dashboard panels (Grafana dashboard ref: grafana/redwood/canary-47321)
E2E tests: step progression, metric gating, and rollback simulation
acceptance_criteria: Rulebook schema published and documented in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Rulebook+Spec
API accepts and validates rulebook manifests and returns descriptive errors
Controller emits signed split deltas and router applies splits in staging cluster
Shadow mode mirrors sampled requests to candidate model without affecting production responses
Auto-rollback occurs in staging when synthetic or real metrics cross defined thresholds (verified in test harness)
telemetry: Emit per-rule metrics: current_step, desired_split_percent, step_start_ts, step_duration_s, canary_health_score, rollback_count. Tag metrics with model_id, route_id, and environment. Dashboards must surface a timeline and per-step metric breakdown.
